newsitem.title: FRANCE: Judge orders suspected Basque separatist to Paris.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders suspected Basque separatist to Paris.

text.p: A book merchant detained in southwestern France on suspicion of supporting the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA has been flown to Paris at the request of an anti-terrorism judge, police said on Thursday.
They said Jean-Louis Maitia, manager of a bookstore specialising in Basque literature, was flown to the capital under a police escort on Wednesday.
He was one of six suspected ETA supporters rounded up this week in a series of raids in the French Basque region and later detained by police.

Among the six was the wife of Henry Unai, also known as Parot, who has been sentenced in Spain to more than 2,000 years in prison for guerrilla activities on behalf of ETA, police said. The woman's name was not released.
France has pledged increased cooperation with Spain in cracking down on ETA, also known as Basque Homeland and Freedom.
The group has killed about 800 people in Spain in its 28-year-old fight for Basque independence.
